phase_name: voice path hardening + morph speed UX

completed_tasks.name: Single-counter voice path (PS1-faithful)
completed_tasks.details: Replaced dual decim_counter/gauss_counter with one voice_counter. Bits 12+ = sample advancement, bits 4-11 = Gaussian index. Matches real PS1 SPU hardware architecture.

completed_tasks.name: Fast/Slow morph speed toggle
completed_tasks.details: Mauve button strip above speed knob. Fast: 0–0.5s. Slow: 0.5–8s. Slow range creates evolving feedback textures during morph transitions.

completed_tasks.name: Gaussian interpolation defaults ON
completed_tasks.details: Real PS1 always runs Gauss — no bypass in hardware. Toggle remains for A/B comparison.

completed_tasks.name: Golden files regenerated
completed_tasks.details: All 80 goldens (50 reverb + 30 ADPCM) regenerated for single-counter output.

human_actions_pending.action: Rebuild beta artifacts with single-counter voice path + Fast/Slow + Gauss-on defaults
human_actions_pending.context: Current beta builds on ~/Desktop are from the dual-counter era. Need rebuild before distributing.

decisions.rationale: Real PS1 SPU uses one pitch counter for both decode and interpolation. Dual-counter produced 98%+ sample divergence vs hardware-faithful architecture.
PS1 hardware always runs Gauss — no bypass exists. Off-by-default was a textbook-DSP instinct, not hardware-faithful.
Slow mode creates evolving feedback textures during transitions. 8s is the sweet spot — long enough for bubbling/crusty effects, short enough to avoid runaway feedback instability.

decisions.decision: AA filter stays but is non-default
decisions.rationale: Real PS1 has no AA filter on the voice decimation path. ADPCM codec band-limits naturally. AA filter is opt-in creative toggle only.

next_action: Rebuild beta plugin artifacts (all 3 platforms) with single-counter voice path + Fast/Slow morph + Gauss-on defaults. Then distribute to testers.
context_notes: Started from signal flow discussion. Identified dual-counter voice path as non-faithful to PS1 hardware. Research confirmed PS1 uses single pitch counter (bits 12+ = sample index, bits 4-11 = Gauss index). Implemented, tested, verified. Then added Fast/Slow morph speed after Anthony identified the slow morph transitions as 'secret sauce' — tried 60s (feedback blowup), 1.5s (too short), 5s (good), landed on 8s ceiling.
